Box Office Update: 'You Can See Everything' and 'Clayface' Battle for Top Spot Over Sluggish Halloween Weekend

A Tight Race for the Weekend Lead

As the Halloween weekend draws to a close, a close competition has emerged for the top spot at the domestic box office between A24’s documentary *You Can See Everything* and Warner Bros.’ DC film *Clayface*. Reports indicate both titles are contending for the lead, with early figures placing their weekend grosses in the $10 million to $11 million range.

Box Office Performance Highlights

  • You Can See Everything: The three-hour documentary, co-directed by Lance Oppenheim and featuring Nathan Fielder and Elizabeth Holmes, is showing strong performance in hourly ticket sales, particularly among its core audience of older female moviegoers. It has already surpassed the lifetime domestic grosses of several notable documentaries, including *Bowling for Columbine* and *An Inconvenient Truth*.
  • Clayface: The James Watkins-directed Batman villain spinoff faces a significant drop in its second weekend, estimated at roughly 57% to 69% depending on the specific reporting source, as it competes for the number one spot.
  • Market Context: The overall weekend performance across all titles is estimated at $62.2 million, a 38% decrease from the previous week, marking one of the lowest-grossing weekends of 2026.

Additional Noteworthy Releases

  • Wildwood: The Laika-produced, Fathom-released film continues to maintain a steady presence in the top five, with an estimated $7.49 million for the weekend.
  • Wicker: Black Bear’s R-rated comedy has seen improved traction in its second weekend, expanding its theater count and earning praise from audiences, despite the broader industry trend of a slow holiday period.
  • New Openings: Briarcliff Entertainment’s *Christmas at the Kringles* saw a limited release at 1,825 locations, facing difficult critical reception.

Industry Outlook

Box office analysts have noted that the timing of Halloween—falling on a weekend—frequently correlates with slower consumer activity in theaters compared to other frames. While major studios have largely avoided wide releases during this window, independent and specialty titles continue to find footing with specific demographics. Industry participants expect finalized box office results to emerge early next week as theater reports are reconciled.

Readers interested in tracking official weekend tallies can verify figures through standard industry box office reporting services such as Comscore or by monitoring major trade publications that aggregate studio-reported data.
